stories.headline: Madurantakam by-election: Will the AIADMK ‘bastion’ fall to TVK’s growing popularity?
stories.title: Madurantakam by-election: Will the AIADMK ‘bastion’ fall to TVK’s growing popularity?
stories.summary: Maragatham Kumaravel, a former AIADMK leader, now seeks re-election as the TVK’s candidate after resigning as AIADMK MLA barely three weeks after the 2026 result; while some voters are undecided, some say they may not vote for the TVK despite the CM’s popularity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In the 2021 Assembly Elections, the ruling AIADMK was swept away by a DMK wave in the KTCC districts (Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, and Chennai), barring one single seat – Madurantakam.
Maragatham Kumaravel, a seasoned AIADMK leader and a Lok Sabha member for the party during 2014-19 period, stood tall among the ruins.
She regained the seat in the 2026 elections amid a TVK wave in the region, giving rise to claims that it was an AIADMK bastion.
Then came the twist.
Barely three weeks after the declaration of results, Ms. Maragatham, along with five of her colleagues, resigned from the Assembly and joined the TVK.
She is now recast as the TVK candidate for the Madurantakam by-election scheduled for October 6.
On Friday, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay held a four-and-a-half-hour-long roadshow in the constituency.
People lined up in large numbers all along the route, which crisscrossed the constituency touching about three dozen villages.
If the turnout of people translates to votes for the party, the TVK would win.
But often, what is apparent isn’t real, warns Ashok, a grocery store owner in Ayyanar Nagar.
“Not all those who gather at Vijay’s rallies would vote for TVK.
I went there too to catch a glimpse of him but I may not vote for them,” he states.

stories.headline: India GDP growth forecast stays at 7%: Virmani
stories.title: India GDP growth forecast stays at 7%: Virmani
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: “My forecast right now for the whole year is still the same.
7% plus or minus 1%,” Virmani told ANI on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave.

Virmani said he had earlier raised his growth forecast from 6.5% to 7% but had simultaneously widened the uncertainty range, stressing that uncertainty is an inherent feature of macroeconomic conditions.
“Uncertainty is a fact of macroeconomic life,” he said, noting that economic forecasts can be affected by developments that were not anticipated when projections were made.
He said he had reassessed his forecast about a month ago in light of unresolved trade issues and other global factors, but decided to retain the 7% projection.
Virmani said he would not revise his full-year estimate solely on the basis of quarterly GDP data, despite India recording 7.8% growth in the first quarter of FY27.
“A lot of people saw this 7.8 and suddenly started raising their forecasts.
But I don't do that.
I have a forecast, I have a range of uncertainty,” he said.

His comments come as economists and analysts reassess India's growth outlook following the stronger-than-expected first-quarter expansion, while external factors including trade developments remain a source of uncertainty.

On the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for UPI transactions, Virmani said the initial subsidy had played an important role in expanding UPI and creating what he described as a new public good, but argued that the system should gradually move towards a cost-based model.
“A good subsidy creates a new public good at minimum cost,” he said.
